source_text: E regione Cain, invidus, parricida, de eadem natura progenitus, non eadem voluntate provectus, excarnificante animum tremore vastatur. Ergo in hunc mundum peccatum intrasse per unum Apostolus dixit et per peccatum mortem et ita in omnes homines mortem pertransisse, qui peccaverunt. Quae sententia catholico dogmati conveniens nihil vobis impertit auxilii.
pass_a_gloss: From the opposite region Cain, envious, a parricide, begotten from the same nature, not advanced by the same will, is laid waste by a trembling that flays the soul. The Apostle therefore said that sin entered into this world through one and through sin death and so death passed through into all human beings who sinned. Which sentence, agreeing with catholic dogma, imparts no help to you.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: On the opposite side, Cain—envious and a murderer of his brother, born from the same nature but developing through a different will—is ravaged by trembling that tears his soul apart (Genesis 4:8–14, following the Greek/Old Latin description of his trembling). Thus the apostle said that sin entered this world through one man, and death through sin, and that death so passed into all human beings who sinned (Romans 5:12). This statement agrees with catholic doctrine and lends you no help.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: The trembling of Cain reflects the Greek/Old Latin form of Genesis 4:12, rather than the “fugitive and wanderer” wording familiar from Hebrew-based translations.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
